name: Enceladus
kicker: Saturn’s icy, geyser-spraying moon · A top place to search for life
briefing: Enceladus is a small, snow-white moon of Saturn, only about 500 kilometers wide, yet spacecraft have caught it erupting. In 2005, the Cassini spacecraft found jets of water vapor and ice shooting out of long cracks near its south pole, nicknamed “tiger stripes.” Those jets come from a salty ocean hidden under the ice, which makes this little moon one of the best places to search for life beyond Earth.

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Features on this moon are named for people and places in _The Arabian Nights_. Craters there honor characters like Ali Baba and Aladdin, and four long, parallel fractures near its south pole are named for Alexandria, Cairo, Baghdad, and Damascus.
tossups.r: Those fractures, nicknamed “tiger stripes,” spray water ice into space. For 10 points, name this geyser-spouting moon of Saturn.

tossups.p: William Herschel discovered this moon in 1789 with his giant new 40-foot telescope, a few weeks before he found its neighbor Mimas [“MY-mus”]. Decades later, his son John named it for a Giant of Greek myth who was buried beneath Mount Etna.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small, icy moon of Saturn whose south pole sprays plumes of water.

tossups.p: This moon completes two orbits for every one orbit of Dione [“dy-OH-nee”], a pattern that keeps its path slightly stretched. As a result, Saturn’s tides keep flexing this moon and heating its interior, which helps keep water liquid beneath its icy shell.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this moon of Saturn whose hidden ocean feeds plumes erupting from its “tiger stripes.”

tossups.p: In 2015, scientists announced that this moon wobbles slightly as it orbits, too much for an icy shell frozen solid all the way down to its rocky core. The wobble showed that a global ocean separates this moon’s crust from its core.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this moon of Saturn, whose south-pole geysers were discovered by the Cassini spacecraft.

tossups.p: In 2017, NASA announced that molecular hydrogen in this moon’s spray may come from hot water reacting with rock on its seafloor, a possible energy source for microbes like those living at Earth’s deep-sea vents. Tiny grains of silica had already pointed to such hydrothermal activity.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this ice-covered moon of Saturn, a top target in the search for life.

tossups.p: Voyager 2 photos from 1981 showed that large parts of this moon have almost no craters, a sign that those areas are geologically young. Astronomers also suspected this moon of supplying a faint ring that is densest along its orbit.
tossups.r: That is the E ring. For 10 points, name this bright, icy moon of Saturn that sprays water from its south pole.

tossups.p: In early 2005, Cassini’s magnetometer noticed Saturn’s magnetic field bending around this moon as if it had a thin atmosphere. Mission planners then sent the spacecraft much closer to find where that gas was coming from.
tossups.r: It came from plumes of water vapor and ice erupting near the south pole. For 10 points, name this moon of Saturn.

tossups.p: In October 2015, the Cassini spacecraft dove through the spray erupting from this moon’s south pole, passing less than 50 kilometers above its surface. Over many flybys, Cassini found water vapor, carbon dioxide, methane, and organic molecules in that spray.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this moon of Saturn whose geysers shoot from cracks called “tiger stripes.”

tossups.p: In 2023, NASA announced that the James Webb Space Telescope had spotted a plume of water vapor from this moon stretching thousands of kilometers into space, many times wider than the moon itself. Some of that water spreads into a doughnut-shaped cloud around its planet.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this icy moon of Saturn, which sprays water from cracks near its south pole.

tossups.p: In 2023, scientists studying ice grains that this moon had sprayed into space found phosphates, the first sign of phosphorus in an ocean beyond Earth. Phosphorus is a key ingredient of DNA and of the molecules that carry energy inside living cells.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this moon of Saturn, which hides an ocean beneath its icy surface.

tossups.p: Rather than risk the spacecraft someday crashing into this moon, which might harbor life, mission controllers sent Cassini plunging into Saturn in 2017. Three years earlier, measurements of this moon’s gravity had pointed to a sea of liquid water beneath its south pole.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small moon of Saturn whose geysers feed the planet’s faint E ring.

tossups.p: Along with Neptune’s moon Triton, this moon is one of the few icy worlds where spacecraft have caught active eruptions, a kind of activity called cryovolcanism. Cassini identified about 100 separate jets on this moon, all lined up along four warm fractures.
tossups.r: Those fractures are nicknamed “tiger stripes.” For 10 points, name this geyser-spouting moon of Saturn.

tossups.p: This moon has one of the highest albedos in the solar system, reflecting most of the sunlight that hits it, partly because fine ice crystals from its own eruptions keep falling back onto its surface like fresh snow.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this bright, white moon of Saturn whose geysers spray from “tiger stripes.”

tossups.p: Scientists say this moon offers three main ingredients for life as we know it: liquid water, a source of energy, and carbon-based chemistry. A proposed NASA mission called Orbilander would orbit this moon, then land on it to study material from its plumes.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small moon of Saturn, which sprays water from an underground ocean.

tossups.p: Salt-rich ice grains caught by Cassini’s Cosmic Dust Analyzer showed that this moon’s spray must come from liquid salt water rather than from solid ice. Grains from that spray also make up most of a faint, wide ring around its planet.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small moon of Saturn with “tiger stripes” near its south pole.

trap.title: Which ocean moon?
trap.body: Three icy moons with hidden oceans show up again and again in quiz bowl. Titan is Saturn’s biggest moon, with a thick orange atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane, and Europa circles Jupiter. Players also hear “Saturn” or “Cassini” and blurt out the planet, but a question that says “this moon” wants the moon.
trap.fix: Tiny and bright, “tiger stripes,” south-pole geysers, the E ring, Herschel’s 1789 discovery, the Dione resonance, and names from _The Arabian Nights_ mean Enceladus. A thick haze, methane lakes, or the Huygens probe mean Titan. Jupiter, Galileo, and Europa Clipper mean Europa.
